name: ecasound
desc: Multitrack-capable audio recorder and effect processor
why: A scriptable multitrack recorder and effects chain with an old-school command-line instrument feel.

brief.what_it_is: Ecasound is a software package for multitrack audio processing, covering simple jobs like playback, recording and format conversion as well as multitrack effect processing, mixing, and signal recycling. Its effects and audio objects can be combined in various ways, and their parameters can be driven by operator objects such as oscillators and MIDI-CCs. It ships with a console-mode user interface. The homepage does not describe concrete input and output formats beyond saying it supports a wide range of audio inputs, outputs and effect algorithms.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a general-purpose tool for multitrack audio processing, from simple playback and conversion up to multitrack effects, mixing and recording. It gives no more specific problem statement.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the homepage gives no setup steps, runtime or account requirements. The brew metadata lists these executables: ecaconvert, ecafixdc, ecalength, ecamonitor, ecanormalize, ecaplay, ecasignalview, ecasound, libecasound-config, libecasoundc-config. Windows support is limited to Cygwin, per the homepage.
brief.standout: It is a long-running, scriptable command-line audio tool with a console interface and operator objects such as oscillators and MIDI-CC controllers that can drive effect parameters. The brew package also bundles a family of small single-purpose ecа* utilities alongside the main binary.
brief.status: Probably quiet. The homepage's latest release is 2.9.3, dated 11.01.2020, and the newest news item is from that same date. Earlier releases were 2.9.2 (16.06.2019) and 2.9.1 (03.01.2014). The copyright line reads 1999-2020. I did not check a repository commit history, so this is an inference from the site, not a confirmed abandonment.
brief.caveats: Primary platform is GNU/Linux. It also runs on FreeBSD, Mac OS X and Solaris. Windows support is limited, through Cygwin only. Licensed under the GNU GPL. The homepage's latest release is more than five years old, so check whether it still builds and runs cleanly on current systems. The brew metadata has an empty caveats field.
